heroHeadline: UN Adds Israel to Blacklist for Conflict-Related Sexual Violence; IDF Kills Second Hamas Qassam Brigades Chief in 12 Days
heroSubtitle: Israeli forces struck Hamas's newly appointed Qassam Brigades chief Mohammed Odeh in Rimal, Gaza City on May 26, killing him along with his wife, son, and three others — the second Hamas military wing chief eliminated in 12 days after IDF killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad on May 15. Defense Minister Katz confirmed the kill on May 27. A separate IDF strike on the Tel al-Sultan displacement camp in Rafah on the same day (Eid al-Adha) killed at least 45 people sheltering in tents, triggering a serious Egypt-Israel border incident in which an Egyptian soldier was killed at a Rafah watchtower after an Israeli armored vehicle crossed the boundary line — the most significant bilateral incident between the two countries since October 2023. France formally banned National Security Minister Ben-Gvir from entry (joining Poland and Canada), while the post-ceasefire Palestinian death toll surpassed 1,000+ since October 2025. Israeli coalition politics continued to fracture as Haredi parties rejected a compromise draft exemption bill, making September 2026 elections the most likely outcome.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, Middle East Eye, CNN, The National, Euronews, CBC News, NBC News, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
